reasons.text: Both parts describe the same copper ground strap: the same part type, material, size, unit of measure, make/buy and business unit, with weights about 2% apart.
Their export classifications conflict: one is 9A991 and the other is 9A610.x, a more tightly controlled military-related classification, so a merge could misclassify the surviving part.
If the parts are confirmed to be the same, 100-008565 would normally be kept because it is used in more assemblies, even though 330-007522 is older and both are released.

before_merging: Have export compliance decide which classification applies to this strap (9A991 vs 9A610.x) and whether 330-007522 was classified 9A610.x for a specific military program.
Ask D. Mehta and C. Lindqvist whether the two straps are physically and functionally identical.
Check the recorded weights: a 310 x 20 x 2 mm copper strap should weigh roughly 0.11 kg, so both values (about 2.2 kg) look wrong and should be corrected.
Review the 4 assemblies using 100-008565 and the 3 using 330-007522 to make sure replacing one with the other does not change the export status of any assembly.
